title: The Rhythm Club and Local 802
summary: He describes the musicians-only Rhythm Club and union.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Now, the club, I've forgotten, the club that you hung out in, all the musicians hung out.
The Rhythm Club. Yes, tell me, what was that like? What happened there?
In there, the Rhythm Club, they open in there, sometimes don't close at all. And the floor, you walk

in and they had a piano, baby grand, so different guys come in there and play, sometimes they'd jam and sometimes they'd jam. In the back they had a pool table and they had a poker table, too, like a casino. And nothing but musicians.
No, it was a -- the Rhythm Club, nothing but musicians over there.
Yeah. So it wasn't open to the public.

No, no, no, strictly musicians. You used to belong to the club, and that's the man that brought the Negro musician to the (unintelligible). I came with that (unintelligible). It was a club around somewhere, and they had kitchens. So they brought all this colored musicians from the Rhythm Club into 802.
So 802 came in from the Rhythm Club.
But everything was already organized. It was strictly a white local.
So this band -- the man who used to own that club, he was a very influential man. I think he was (unintelligible), too, somewhere around there, I don't know.
And he brought all these musicians to (unintelligible) in Chicago.
